thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 PagerDuty P1 -> Network flap detected in AZ az1a. Multiple ENI probe failures causing TCP resets and elevated 5xx rates for inference fleet inf-prod-az1a. Triggered by increased ENI DETACH/REATTACH events. Root TS: 3329998888

anna_oncall: seeing spike in 5xx, latency 95p from 120ms -> 700ms for online-gen endpoints. confirming on dashboards now.

sam_net: seeing ENI detach events from AWS controlplane logs, roughly 1 every 30s across the AZ. probelist indicates upstream NBMA errors.

miguel_runtime: KV cache miss rate up 8% for az1a, token latencies spiking. traffic routed to az1b but some flows sticky to az1a due to client affinity.

anna_oncall: quick checklist: 1) throttle new allocations in az1a, 2) shift routing for inference API to prefer az1b/az1c, 3) start canary smaller model fallback to reduce load. doing 1 and 2 now.

ops-bot: runbook reminder: https://playbooks.redwood/eni-flap -> follow step 1-6 for soft-eviction and cross-az steering.

sam_net: AWS console shows short-lived API throttling to ENI attach endpoints; suspect control-plane instability in az1a. filing ticket with AWS now.

miguel_runtime: implementing runtime fallbacks: updating routing policy to mark az1a as degraded and applying immediate model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive routes. patching config: 

```
# route policy patch (runtime)
priority: region,preferred_az: [az1b,az1c,az1a]
sticky_session_ttl: 30s
model_fallbacks:
  - name: small-latency
    max_tokens: 512
    target: az1b
```

anna_oncall: executed routing change, traffic shifted ~82% off az1a within 90s. 5xx rate trending down but not fully resolved.

tara_support: customer-impact check: filtering logs for customers with >3% error rate in last 10m. prepping customer note draft.

kevin_product: need to know if any config changes will affect SLAs or usage reporting. keep me posted.

sam_net: AWS replied - they're seeing increased ENI attach latency due to internal controlplane backlog, affecting our AZ capacity requests. they've escalated to networking team. ETA unknown.

anna_oncall: mitigation plan update: 1) keep traffic steering to other AZs for next 30m, 2) drain unhealthy instances in az1a gracefully, 3) enable cross-AZ autoscale to cover capacity shortfall, 4) send initial customer notice. executing drain now.

miguel_runtime: draining nodes: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running | grep az1a
kubectl cordon <node-from-az1a>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```
Drain started at 3329999001.

anna_oncall: drain progressing, some pods are stuck due to long-lived model loads (80s). miguel, can we force-evict with graceful 15s?

miguel_runtime: forcing with SIGTERM+15s, then SIGKILL. doing now. expect brief extra errors as model processes shutdown.

ops-bot: reaction :thumbsup: from incident-bot recorded.

tara_support: sending proactive note to customers in impacted regions: 
"We detected elevated errors and latency for requests routed to AZ az1a starting ~12:12 UTC. We've shifted traffic to alternate AZs and are draining affected nodes. You may see transient 5xx or higher latency for in-progress requests. We'll update in 30 minutes."

kevin_product: thanks. also track token accounting — shifted traffic should not double-charge. confirm with billing ops.

sam_net: temporary routing change: updated L4 steering rules to prefer other AZs and reduce new ENI allocations in az1a. applied at 3329999105.

anna_oncall: monitoring metrics: 5xx from 6.2% -> 1.1% after shift; p95 latency back to ~180ms. still seeing sporadic resets (approx 0.3% of requests).

miguel_runtime: enabling additional KV cache warmup in fallback AZs to reduce cold misses. queueing background preload job: 
```
POST /internal/cache/warmup
{ "scope": "top-100-prompts", "target_az": ["az1b","az1c"] }
```

sam_net: AWS says they will continue to monitor controlplane; if backlog persists they may move capacity, but could be expensive. recommend we keep steering until steady for 1h.

anna_oncall: agree. set incident status -> INVESTIGATING / MITIGATED (partial) at 3329999200. oncall handing off to night-shift at 3329999220.

miguel_runtime: runtime metrics look stable in fallback AZs. starting gradual rollback of model fallback for lower-cost endpoints only. will keep latency-first routes on fallback until confirmed stable.

ops-bot: Handoff checklist: include summary, actions taken, current state, and next steps.

anna_oncall: summary for handoff: 
- Root cause: AWS ENI attach/controlplane backlog in az1a resulting in probe flaps and ENI detaches.
- Impact: transient TCP resets and elevated 5xx for inference endpoints (~peak 6.2%).
- Actions: routing pref to az1b/az1c, drained unhealthy nodes in az1a, applied model fallbacks, warmed KV caches, contacted AWS.
- Current state: 5xx ~1.1%, p95 ~180ms, traffic ~18% still in az1a (sticky sessions), AWS monitoring.
- Next steps: monitor for 1h, if events continue escalate to AWS higher tier, keep steering.

tara_support: sent customer note 3329999215. will follow up with impacted accounts individually.

kevin_product: assign communication owner for post-incident summary? tara_support will draft and I will review.

anna_oncall: handing off to night oncall @miguel_runtime for monitoring and rollback plan. tagging pager: @miguel_runtime.

miguel_runtime: taking handoff. I'll keep traffic steering until 3330002500 (approx +55m) or until AWS confirms controlplane stable.

incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0421-az1a-eni-flap. Severity P1. Postmortem requested within 48h.

end of thread.
